prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

TEXT_D:
The Liberal Democrats’ Real Alternative is a costed, green, liberal programme built on Freedom, Fairness and Trust, with power devolved from Westminster and a strong internationalist outlook. A “green thread” runs throughout.

Fair, simple, affordable government
- Fully costed plans, switching around £5bn a year from low-priority spend (abolish unnecessary subsidies and the DTI’s wasteful functions; scrap ID cards; redirect the Child Trust Fund) to frontline priorities.
- One net tax rise: a 50% rate only on income over £100,000 to fund abolishing tuition and top-up fees, free personal care for the elderly and disabled, and lower local taxes.
- Replace the unfair Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay, saving the typical household about £450 a year; raise the stamp duty threshold to £150,000.

Putting patients first
- Free personal care for older and disabled people; more doctors, nurses and therapists; sweep away pointless central targets so clinicians and locally accountable bodies decide.
- Faster diagnosis via the quickest practical route; expand scans/tests (evenings/weekends), publish diagnostic waits.
- Free eye and dental checks; extend prescription charge exemptions; rebuild NHS dentistry; legislate for better mental health rights; ban smoking in enclosed public places; hardwire prevention and clean environments into health.

Ambitious for every child and learner
- Abolish tuition/top-up fees; restore fair grants; equalise college/school funding; modernise skills with a 14–19 diploma blending vocational and academic routes.
- Cut infant class sizes to an average of 20 (junior to 25) by hiring 21,000 teachers; extend wraparound care and complete 3,500 Children’s Centres.
- Less high-stakes testing; strengthen discipline and SEND support.

Tackling crime, defending liberty
- 10,000 more police by cancelling ID cards; cut red tape so officers patrol, not paperwork.
- Smart justice: tough community penalties for non-violent offenders; focus on traffickers and acquisitive crime.
- Repeal control-order regime; defend jury trial; prosecute terror in open courts (including intercept evidence); create a UK Border Force.
- Fair asylum decisions by a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work; Single Equality Act and hate-crime units; specialist Environmental Tribunal.

Prosperity with less red tape, more green growth
- Independent budget scrutiny by the NAO; simpler, fairer business taxes; small-business rate relief; “sunset clauses” on regulation; duty to trade fairly; boost tourism.
- Green fiscal reform: shift to a Carbon Tax; incentives for efficient homes/clean vehicles; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; do not replace ageing nuclear; promote hydrogen and clean tech.

Security, rights and global leadership
- Iraq was wrong; rebuild through the UN/EU, include Sunnis, strengthen Iraqi forces, and aim to withdraw UK troops with the UN mandate’s expiry.
- Support EU reform and the Constitution via referendum; prepare to join the euro when conditions are right; managed economic migration.
- Right-size procurement (cut Eurofighter Tranche 3) to fund troops’ welfare; retain a minimum nuclear deterrent while driving multilateral disarmament; tighten arms export controls.

Fair pensions and support
- Citizen’s Pension from 75 with earnings link (ending means-testing for around a million); Local Income Tax benefits eight in ten pensioners; £170/week Maternity Income Guarantee for six months; scrap the CSA and move enforcement to HMRC; extend Winter Fuel Payment to severely disabled adults; robust anti-fraud simplification.

Stronger local communities, rural fairness, better transport
- Devolve power, cut inspectorates to a streamlined Audit Commission; protect post offices and universal mail.
- Release public land to build 100,000 affordable homes; favour brownfield; control second homes where markets are distorted.
- Fair farm/food trading (Food Trade Inspector); CAP reform for public goods; Marine Act; Animal Welfare Commission; strict GM safeguards, promote organic.
- Fix rail with fewer, longer franchises and key upgrades; reward cleaner cars; expand congestion charging with upfront transit investment; plan national road-user charging to replace fuel/vehicle taxes; limit new roads; greener aviation taxes; free off-peak buses for pensioners/disabled and free railcards for target groups.

Better government
- Curb Prime Ministerial power (War Powers Act; Civil Service Act); predominantly elected second chamber; STV for all elections and votes at 16; deeper devolution; independent BBC regulator; Environmental Responsibility Act and a unified Environment–Transport–Energy department.

Climate leadership
- Beat UK Kyoto targets early; lead toward “contraction and convergence”; scale renewables, efficiency and recycling; help households cut bills and carbon.

TEXT_C:
The Green Party’s 2005 manifesto sets out a realistic, values-driven programme for social, economic and environmental justice—putting people and planet before short-term profit, reversing privatisation, tackling inequality, and confronting climate change. It champions democracy, peace and localisation to build shared prosperity and long-term security.

- Economics: Tackle inequality with more progressive income tax bands, higher Corporation Tax for large firms, a progressive inheritance tax on recipients, and abolition of National Insurance in favour of broader income taxation. Pilot a Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates. Replace VAT with revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes that price resource use, waste and pollution. Back small firms, co‑ops and community banks; promote credit unions and local currencies; oppose UK entry to the euro; reform global trade rules. Create green jobs and defend workers’ rights; measure real progress beyond GDP.

- Energy and climate: Adopt Contraction and Convergence, cutting UK CO2 by 20% by 2010 on a path to 85% by 2030. Replace VAT/CCL on energy with a Carbon Tax, protecting low users. Reach 40% renewables by 2020 through major investment in wind, solar, wave and biogas, and shift R&D from nuclear to renewables. Cut demand via a Warmer Homes Act and Smart Energy Councils. Decommission nuclear as stations reach end of life.

- Welfare: Phase in a universal, non‑withdrawable Citizen’s Income to replace most means‑tested benefits; retain and then integrate housing benefit; keep disability/incapacity benefits additional. Establish a universal Citizen’s Pension linked to earnings, replacing Pension Credit. Support families by simplifying child support, raising Child Benefit, reducing working hours, and expanding Sure Start. Boost affordable housing through council building, self‑build co‑ops, LVT, and energy efficiency.

- Health and education: Restore the NHS to universal, comprehensive, publicly provided care; end PFI/PPP and foundation hospitals; oppose GATS in public services. Abolish prescription, eye test and dental charges; expand access to holistic care. Raise health spending to at least 9% of GNP, with a hypothecated NHS tax. In education, fund lifelong learning, expand pre‑school, scrap tuition fees and restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs and move toward Individual Learning Plans.

- Transport: Prioritise walking, cycling and public transport; cut road traffic 10% by 2010; re‑regulate buses; return rail and tube to public ownership; expand rail and light rail. Reflect true costs of motoring via congestion/road pricing, higher fuel duty and freight levies; invest in clean vehicle R&D. Resist airport expansion, ban night flights, and tax aviation fuel/emissions.

- Environment: Commit to Zero Waste with a ban on incineration, a national agency, and 60% recycling by 2010. Levy eco‑taxes on polluting inputs; create an Environmental Protection Commission. Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation and nanotech; oppose patents on genetic resources; strengthen animal welfare (end live exports, ban battery eggs, curb fur; replace vivisection).

- Food and farming: Pass an Organics Target Bill (30% by 2012); replace CAP/CFP with support for organic, local and biodiversity‑enhancing systems; ban GM food; curb supermarket market power.

- Crime and justice: Prevent crime by strengthening communities—better urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, treating drugs as a health issue; oppose ID cards. Expand accountable community policing. Enact strict gun controls. Embed restorative justice. Tackle hate crime, violence against women, and disability discrimination.

- Democracy: Renew local government with stronger powers, PR for councils and Westminster, referenda and recall; elected House of Lords; a written constitution, disestablishment of the Church, and curbed royal powers. Devolve regionally; enhance Scottish/Welsh powers. Oppose an undemocratic EU constitution while pursuing EU reform.

- Peace and international policy: Pursue an ethical foreign policy; oppose the Iraq war, replace UK troops with UN peacekeepers. Cut defence to the EU average; end arms export subsidies; back an Arms Trade Treaty; decommission nuclear weapons. Raise aid to at least 1% of GNI; cancel debts of the 52 poorest countries; support a Tobin tax. Reform the UN (end permanent Security Council seats) and democratise IMF/World Bank. Replace/transform WTO rules with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade favouring localisation, fairness and environmental limits. Uphold asylum rights: benefits, right to work, independent appeals; ratify migrant and refugee conventions.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile.
